results.title: A systematic review of influences on engagement with remote health interventions targeting weight management for individuals living with excess weight | International Journal of Obesity
results.content: # A systematic review of influences on engagement with remote health interventions targeting weight management for individuals living with excess weight. Previous reviews have investigated influential factors to engagement of such interventions in community settings; however, limited research has examined adults’ engagement in remote weight management programmes. ### Aim. To systematically review the influences on the engagement of adults living with excess weight in synchronous (real time), remote health interventions for weight management. Studies were included if they delivered a synchronous, remote weight management intervention with participants that were ≥18 years old with a body mass index ≥27.5 kg/m2. A total of 57 themed influences were iteratively coded and mapped to the COM-B model: physical capability (*n* = 2); psychological capability (*n* = 10), reflective motivation (*n* = 17); automatic motivation (*n* = 10); physical opportunity (*n* = 7); and social opportunity (*n* = 11) with the assistance of the TDF to guide the coding. ### The effectiveness of social-support-based weight-loss interventions—a systematic review and meta-analysis.
